summary: Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1875–1879) and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (~1881–1882). He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1880–1886) and professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

An Indologist and linguist, Edward Washburn Hopkins studied at Columbia University (~1874–1878) and Leipzig University under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch (~1880–1881, Ph.D.). He held posts at Columbia, Bryn Mawr College (1885–1895), and Yale University (1895–1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied as a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under traditional teachers Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

Active in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology, Edwin Arnold studied at King's College London and the University of Oxford. He served as a schoolmaster at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and became Principal of Poona Sanskrit College/Deccan College in 1856.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1858–1861), served as President of the Asiatic Society (1886–1887), and was Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

Edwin Francis Bryant works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1990–1997), taught at Harvard University (~1998–2003), and was appointed Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University (~2003).

Edwin Gerow was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1985–1997) and as Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1993–1997).

Active in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology, Edwin Norris worked at the East India Company (1818–1837) and the Foreign Office (1847–1866). He also served as assistant secretary (1836) and Assistant-Honorary Secretary and Honorary Librarian (1856–1861) at the Royal Asiatic Society.

Edwin Whitfield Fay was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins University (Ph.D.), and Leipzig University under Maurice Bloomfield and others. He held professorships at Washington and Lee University (1893–1899) and the University of Texas.

Egaku Maeda specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen University Junior College, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

Egil Asprem is a religious studies scholar who studied at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (~2003–2008) and the University of Amsterdam (~2008–2013). He has held posts at NTNU, UC Santa Barbara, and Stockholm University.

Eido Shimano was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa, and attended the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and master at New York Zendo Shobo-ji.

Eiichi Chino was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Harushige Takatsu (~1952–1957). He later held posts at Wako University (~1966–1967), Tokyo University of Education (~1967–1974), and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1974–1993).

Eiichi Imoto worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1950–1958) and later held academic posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1996) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1996–2005).

Eiichi Makino was a scholar of philosophy and law who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903). He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938), Chuo University, Tohoku University, Kyushu University, and Shiraume Gakuen Junior College.
Eiichi Otani is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Toyo University (~1987–1998). He served as professor and dean at Kyoto Bunkyo University (~2004–2010).
Eiichi Yamaguchi studied Indology and philosophy as a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990). He also held a post there as a research assistant (attested 1991).
Eiin Yasuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a disciple under Gyoin Hashimoto (~1950–1973). He completed his university studies at Ryukoku University (~1957–1961).
Eikan Taki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Taisho University. He served as a lecturer at its Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism (attested 2006).

Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1962–1971). He later served at Taisho University as Director and Professor in the Faculty of Humanities (~1980–2013).
